sections.content: How many people are "leisure and travel service occupations (other)"?

11,085 people

were counted on the census as "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work perform a variety of leisure and travel service occupations not elsewhere classified.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 65 years or older. Of the whole working population 4.2% were aged 65 years or older. For people working as "leisure and travel service occupations (other)", 16% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" included:

  • market research interviewers
  • tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out
  • horticultural trades

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" there were a similar number of men and women (54.2% compared with 45.8%).

This means "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "leisure, travel and related personal service occupations".

Men made up 54.2% and women made up 45.8% of "leisure and travel service occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" included:

  • design occupations (other)
  • publicans and managers of licensed premises
  • shelf fillers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "leisure and travel service occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "leisure and travel service occupations (other)", 12.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (59% compared with 41%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (76.8%) than self-employed (23.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wiltshire, this is in the region of the South West.
